stories.headline: The Premier League belongs to Erling Haaland after summer transfer window
stories.summary: The Premier League was once a league of superstars, but after a summer of clubs signing depth over singular talent, Haaland is now the biggest star left, though it hasn't dampened the league's popularity or power one bit.
stories.body:
Noel Gallagher, Zlatan Ibrahimovic, Jack Grealish and a topless Pep Guardiola all reacted with disbelief and laughter when Erling Haaland took to FaceTime so he could show off his fresh haircut.

Millions watched the clip across Haaland's social media platforms, including his own YouTube channel. Gone were the flowing blonde locks; thousands of blonde wigs worn by Haaland fans at the World Cup would need a trim, and the Premier League's preseason promotional hype montages would merit a redo.

One thing, however, hasn't changed: the Premier League is Haaland's league now.

After a summer in which the star power of individual players was showcased at the World Cup, Haaland stood tall among the game's greats. It was the World Cup of Lamine Yamal, Lionel Messi, Kylian Mbappé, Jude Bellingham, Rodri, Harry Kane and Haaland, but of that esteemed group, just the 6-foot-5 Norwegian forward plays in the Premier League.

With the departures of Mohamed Salah (to Trabzonspor), and Son Heung-Min's exit to Major League Soccer the previous summer, Haaland is indisputably the biggest star in the league. It's the same on the touchline. For the first time since the league's inception back in 1992, we have a competition without any superstar manager: Sir Alex Ferguson, Arsene Wenger, Guardiola, Jose Mourinho and Jurgen Klopp are all working elsewhere or out of the coaching game.

But should this come as a concern to the Premier League? Is the world's most dominant league losing appeal, or is it too big to fail?

The Premier League's collective clout
When Sky Sports put together their iconic advert to herald the arrival of the Premier League in 1992, the theme was "a whole new ball game." Set to the backdrop of "Alive and Kicking" by Simple Minds, players from the 22 clubs were engaged in a variety of activities, like joking around in the shower, lifting weights, delivering team talks, enjoying breakfast in bed, or juggling a ball.

It was a statement more than an advert: the Premier League is here. But in terms of global stars, Man United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel was the Premier League's sole representative in the top 30 of the 1992 FIFA World Player of the Year award.

The Premier League platform and its unparalleled reach boosts profiles and nurtures careers -- Cristiano Ronaldo, Thierry Henry, Salah, Kane, Michael Olise, David Beckham, Luka Modric, Eric Cantona, Alan Shearer, Frank Lampard, Gareth Bale and Steven Gerrard all made their names in England's top flight before eventually moving on.

"The popularity of the Premier League is outstretching and leading because of the international interest there is in the game, because over the course of, say, a decade, you'll still see the world's best players in the competition at some stage," Shaun Harvey, non-executive director at Wrexham and former CEO of the EFL and Leeds United, tells ESPN.

There have been occasions where established stars arrive, like Ronaldo's return to Manchester United in 2021, or Zlatan Ibrahimovic's two-year spell at United from 2016-18: both men were globally renowned, but approaching the twilight of their career. The Premier League has had just three Ballon d'Or winners since 1992: Michael Owen (2001), Ronaldo (2008) and Rodri (2024). By and large, the award went to Ronaldo or Messi every time.

"If you are a Premier League administrator, perhaps you might be concerned about the absence of big-name superstars in the league," Simon Chadwick, professor of AfroEurasian sport and specialist in 21st century global sport, tells ESPN. "But at the same time, what I think the Premier League has that other leagues around the world don't have is brand equity in marketing terms," a model not dissimilar from the NFL, where the teams themselves are the draw.

"There's considerable equity in the brands of these clubs, but also considerable fan equity, too."

Regardless, the collective self-assurance of the Premier League remains, 34 years on since it began, and the numbers say as much.

Deloitte's latest "Annual Review of Football Finance" analyses collective revenues of the "big five" leagues and puts the Premier League top, by a comfortable distance: for the 2024-25 season, the Premier League's collective revenue sat at €8.098 billion, with Bundesliga second (€4.3bn), La Liga third (€4.1bn), Serie A fourth (€3bn), and Ligue 1 fifth (€2.2bn).

There are other indicators of its collective strength.

Brand Finance's recently published "Football 50" ranks clubs on their brand value. The Premier League has five teams in their top 10, with Arsenal third behind Real Madrid and Barcelona, and the competitiveness in England continues to attract eager buyers, like the consortium involving Jeff Bezos, who purchased a stake in Liverpool this summer. There's no one-team monopoly like Ligue 1 (with Paris Saint-Germain) or the Bundesliga (Bayern Munich), or a duopoly like Barca and Real Madrid in LaLiga. OPTA's ranking of the strongest leagues in the world puts the Premier League top, ahead of Bundesliga in second and LaLiga third.

"The competitive balance the Premier League has makes it a more enticing league for others overseas," Chadwick says, though Haaland appears to be the exception as a player who attracts as much fandom as any team.

The haircut

Haaland had been warned about potential repercussions of getting rid of his famous blonde locks. "The season starts now so it's time to get a fresh start," Haaland said. "The only thing is, Zlatan [Ibrahimovic] told me never cut your hair, because your strength is in your hair."

Haaland said he was nervous on his livestream, while the hairdresser tasked with the trim said it was "the most expensive haircut of all time." Once the final haircut was revealed, Haaland laughed and said: "I can't wait for the fans to sing 'who the fucking hell is that?'" Then came the FaceTimes and celebrity reactions -- a flex on Haaland's part, but also a valuable insight into his personality and part of the wider strategy around him.

"He's dominating," Steve Martin, founding partner MSQ Sport & Entertainment, tells ESPN. "He's the Premier League's Trojan Horse. He's heavily curated, but what he does is so natural."

Haaland's haircut could be the most famous haircut in the Premier League since Beckham shaved his hair in 2000. Martin worked with Beckham and Adidas on the Predator boots commercials back in 2003 and was behind the famous Beckham link-up with England rugby star -- and World Cup winner -- Jonny Wilkinson.

"There's a machine running all of that, which is where Beckham was so successful and still is for years," Martin says. "It's thought through: there's a PR machine, and it's led by the star themselves. But the beauty of what Haaland is doing is it so authentic. There are parallels with what Beckham did 25 odd years ago. He's got that machine behind it because he's seen the opportunity, but the Beckham or Ronaldo level of fame or social media interest are rare beasts. They're once in a generation, really."

Haaland was one of the faces of the World Cup. He was an already established Champions League and Premier League star, but this summer saw his fanbase grow exponentially as fans watched him engage authentically with the U.S. culture while Norway worked their way through the tournament, whether he was expanding his taxidermy collection or buying a pair of cowboy boots in Texas.

His Instagram follower count alone went from 40.6m to 72.7m, an increase of 32.1m, the most of any player at the World Cup. But of the top 10 players who saw the greatest increase in their Instagram followers this summer, Haaland was the only one from the Premier League, per Sportico.

"His social leap in the World Cup is just unheard of," Martin says. "Obviously there's a lean into increasing his commercial power, but it's very unforced."

Adapting to the young generation
A potential hurdle on the horizon for the Premier League is the rise of how Gen Z and Gen Alpha consume football and the focus on individual players, which a source said was predominantly due to the popularity of EA FC, player's own social media channels and the trading card community.

"The concern is what happens when Haaland leaves," Martin says. "Once you're in the leading position as a league, you need to defend it. Individually, he's in the leadership position, no doubt.

"The Premier League in the past had so much stardust if you like. You had multiple teams with two or three big-name players, but this era is lacking the star power, and the individual players where you're drawn to watching them regardless of who they're playing. I think undoubtedly it could do with a few more global names to carry it into the next era."

However, this trend is nothing new. "I'm convinced in the Premier League and in the UK, fans support teams, not players," Harvey says. "You support your club and they your country, players haven't even been a consideration at that time. They'll have their favourites: fans will get a player on the back of their shirt, but it's a club shirt they buy and wear.

"When you go outside the UK, then there is a lot more prevalence to how do you pick your team in the UK. Fewer fans are peer-pressured by geography, or friends and family influence, into who they support. If you're in the U.S. or the Far East and the Premier League is in front of you, you'll pick your team from what you see on TV.

"You are seeing more new fans picking teams because of a player, and they're more likely to then follow the player as they transfer around, rather than staying loyal to the club. In the UK, fans stay with their club not the player. 'The king is dead, long live the king' is the mantra, and the previous king is likely to be booed when he turns up with the opposition."

The change in the transfer market
Nobody would dispute the fact that individual stars draw a crowd. Look at Inter Miami and how they embraced Messi. Over the summer, we even saw 25,000 delighted fans greet Salah at Trabzonspor. Rodri was unveiled to thousands at the Nou Camp as part of Barcelona's annual squad presentation before the Joan Gamper trophy.

We don't really see those scenes in the Premier League anymore -- certainly nothing like the fiesta Shearer received when he signed for Newcastle in 1996. Players in the Premier League are welcomed on the pitch during the half-time break or before the match -- like Nico González's unveiling at Newcastle -- but you won't see a player juggling on the pitch in a one-off event like you do at the Bernabéu. There, Real Madrid fans are used to seeing Vinicius Jr., Bellingham and Yan Diomande every week. Barcelona boast Yamal, Rodri and Raphinha. PSG enjoy the skills of Ousmane Dembélé and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia -- but all play in leagues whose executives watch the Premier League with understandable envy.

The clubs in the Premier League comfortably outspent any other league in the world this summer. The past transfer window saw the collective spend of the English top flight total at £3.46 billion, but much of that was spent on quality and depth rather than singular star power.

"I think for me, [Premier League clubs] have had a data-driven revolution, which has resulted more of a team-oriented approach to decision-making rather than a star-led or a Galacticos-led model that you see elsewhere in the world," said Chadwick. "These new financial regulations do change the psychology of how teams are assembled and the ways in which clubs are run. Clubs are fascinated by how Brighton and Brentford have done things. You buy low and sell high."

Even when spending big, clubs turn to tried-and-tested options. Out of the top 15 transfers on value, 11 were moves between Premier League clubs; Bradley Barcola's £120m move to Liverpool from PSG was an outlier.

Chadwick feels this is a result of the constraints of Squad Cost Ratio (SCR), a model where club's on-pitch spending is restricted to "85% of their football-related revenue and net profit/loss from player sales," according to the Premier League. Experts feel clubs will spend big on trusted Premier League-proven players. Clubs still spend on potential, and the rise of data and analytics mean these are meticulously planned; expensive gambles like Man United's £86m spend on Antony back in 2022 are a thing of the past.

Of the transfers of players from overseas into the Premier League valued over €35m, just three players were aged over 23. Winger Christos Tzolis (from Club Brugge) had previous experience of the Premier League, defender Piero Hincapié had spent the season on loan at Arsenal (from Bayer Leverkusen) and defensive midfielder Mamadou Sangare (from Lens) is already regarded as one of the purchases of the season. "Clubs are looking for potential -- you don't go looking for current stars," Chadwick says.

Chadwick remembers when his Middlesbrough brought in Juventus star Fabrizio Ravanelli to kick-start the club's push for Europe. He scored, he raised his shirt over his head, and they were relegated. "English football has morphed back into what it always was, which is team-led rather than star-led," Chadwick says.

In turn, this absence of big hitters on the touchline has further reinforced the strength of focus on Haaland.

"I do think that lack of star power on the touchline is a miss for the Premier League," Martin says. "The tension between managers in the past is part of the story. There was great tension between Ferguson and Wenger, then Guardiola and Mourinho. These stories help elevate the whole league."

Still, the Premier League rolls on. "Even players like Ronaldo, Haaland and Messi have a shelf life, but clubs don't -- nor does the Premier League," Chadwick says. "A lot of the noise around the power of players tends to forget that players do get old, they do retire, they do transition to something else. But the clubs and the league remain."

In short, the Premier League is as far-reaching as ever.

"The Premier League is the world's league," Harvey says. And despite a summer where Guardiola and Salah left, its clubs spent collectively more than any other league in the world and will continue to have the most eyeballs on it every single weekend, with Haaland taking up plenty of the spotlight.

"There's absolutely no shortage of quality in the Premier League whatsoever," Premier League CEO Richard Masters said during a preseason sit-down with reporters. "And while we've got a few big names leaving the stage, new stars and new stardust will emerge."

Until then, the floor is Haaland's.

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little ealier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Thursday, Sept. 10

Hogan set to join Pies

GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: Nigeria 'weren't there yet' after FIBA Women's World Cup exit - Rena Wakama
stories.summary: The Nigerian women ended their campaign with a 111-56 loss to France on Monday, their third defeat in as many Group B games after opening with a 99-81 loss to South Korea and then falling 71-67 to Hungary.
stories.body:
Nigeria lasted just three games of the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup, a loss to France in their final group game on Monday sending the African champions crashing out of the tournament.

But coach Rena Wakama says D'Tigress are still rebuilding and "weren't there yet" after a disappointing tournament that ended without a win.

The Nigerian women ended their campaign with a 111-56 loss to France on Monday, their third defeat in as many Group B games after opening with a 99-81 loss to South Korea and then falling 71-67 to Hungary.

While this last defeat to France was somewhat expected, the manner of the loss was sobering for a team that arrived in Berlin two years removed from a historic run to the quarterfinals of the Paris Olympics.

"For us, it's tough because a lot of people saw what we did in 2024, and the reality of where we are today is that we're in a rebuilding process," Wakama said at the post-game press conference.

"I think connectivity is a big thing for myself, my team, my staff. So, where we are today isn't where we were two years ago. And I had to explain that to my team."

France made the gulf between the teams clear almost immediately, racing to a 31-13 lead after the opening quarter and stretching that advantage to 65-26 by halftime.

Nigeria scored 13 points in each of the first three quarters and shot just 28% from the field for the game, while France shot 58%. The French also made a record 22 3-pointers, passing Japan's newly set total of 20 from their defeat of Mali on the opening day. France's Gabby Williams scored 25 points, Janelle Salaun 19 and Marine Johannes 17.

"Huge credit to France," Wakama said. "They are a phenomenal team. A lot of those players are in playoff shape. They play in the WNBA. And my players, we just weren't there yet to be able to compete at the level that they were competing at."

The result completed a sharp reversal from Paris 2024, where Wakama guided Nigeria to victories over Australia and Canada and made D'Tigress the first African basketball team, male or female, to reach an Olympic quarterfinal.

It also represented a step back from Nigeria's last appearance at the Women's World Cup in 2018, when D'Tigress became the first African team to reach the quarterfinals after beating Greece 57-56 in Tenerife.

Nigeria qualified for the 2022 tournament but did not participate after the Nigerian government withdrew the country's national basketball teams from international competition.

This time, there was little momentum from the start.

South Korea opened Nigeria's tournament with a 99-81 victory, with Jihyun Park scoring 27 points. Portland Fire's Amy Okonkwo led D'Tigress with 22 points as Nigeria stayed within three points at halftime before collapsing in the second half and getting outscored 51-36 in the last two quarters.

The opportunity to recover came against Hungary, but Nigeria spent almost the entire game chasing after falling behind 21-13 in the first quarter. Dorka Juhasz finished with 19 points and 16 rebounds as Hungary won 71-67, despite a late Nigerian rally that produced 25 fourth-quarter points.

The overall performance was made even more disappointing because the team had engaged in a whirlwind of preparation that started with training camp in Chicago and games against WNBA teams, to playing three games against China before rounding out their pre-tournament preparations in Europe.

Wakama acknowledged that Nigeria's preparation for the tournament had been good, but said that competing at this level requires more: "We had a great preparation, but I think there's another level that we have to get to in that preparation.

"And huge credit to the NBBF for supporting us and giving us an opportunity to be here, but I know in my mind there is another level we have to get to."

Okonkwo, who had been Nigeria's most productive scorer through the opening two games, was held to just three points against France, missing all eight of her field-goal attempts. She finished with eight rebounds and three assists.

"It was a tough game," Okonkwo said. "France is a great team. We saw it at the 2024 Olympics. We've seen it every qualifier. They are a really great team, and they really came out to play today.

"I think we just struggled to find our rhythm early and we were unable to get the win today or really stop them."

France had also beaten Nigeria 75-54 in the group stage of the Paris Olympics and defeated D'Tigress by a much closer margin of 93-86 when the teams met during the World Cup qualifying tournament in Villeurbanne in March.

Amid the disappointment, Wakama pointed to the silver lining of performances of Nigeria's younger players as one of the positives she will take away from Berlin.

"I'm the most proud of our fight," she said. "When you have a new team, and I have so many young players, I think I have about five or six young players on this team that have never been at this stage before, some that just graduated college.

"Grace Efosa played about 20 minutes. She came on and gave us 15 points. Miriam, these are names you guys will hear in the future. But I threw my young ones in the fire, and they responded for me. So I'm super proud of that."

Grace Efosa-Aguebor's 15 points came in just over 20 minutes and led Nigeria against France. She shot 4 of 7 from the field, including 2 of 4 from 3-point range, and made five of six free throws.

Nigeria leave Berlin 0-3 and bottom of Group B, a result that Wakama believes is as disappointing as it reflects where this version of D'Tigress are compared to what the team accomplished two years ago.

The task now, she says, is finding out what that next version of the team will be: "We can't rely on two years ago's success.

"So who we are today, we're still figuring that out. And I know we will."

stories.headline: Barry Melrose, former player, coach and ESPN analyst, dies
stories.summary: Barry Melrose, a former NHL player and coach who was a beloved, longtime hockey analyst for ESPN, died Wednesday, his wife, Cindy, told ESPN's Steve Levy.
stories.body:
Barry Melrose, a former NHL player and coach who was a beloved hockey analyst for ESPN for over 25 years, died Wednesday, his wife, Cindy, told ESPN's Steve Levy.

He was 70.

Melrose was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in 2023, leading to his retirement from ESPN. He joined the network in 1996.

"For decades, Barry Melrose was one of the most distinctive and trusted voices in hockey," ESPN said in a statement. "His knowledge of the game was deep, his candor was refreshing, and his passion was unmistakable. He was a foundational part of ESPN's hockey coverage, and fans and teammates truly appreciated his entertaining delivery and charismatic personality.

"We send our deepest condolences to his loved ones. He always kept it interesting and he will be missed."

Melrose served as coach of the Wayne Gretzky-led Los Angeles Kings, taking them to the Stanley Cup Final in the first of his three seasons (1992 to 1995). He stepped away briefly from ESPN in 2008 to return to the bench, this time as coach of the Tampa Bay Lightning for 16 games.

Overall, he had an 84-108-29 record as a head coach.

At ESPN, millions watched him as a studio analyst, and within the company's walls, he was lauded as the consummate teammate.

He was known for his witty personality, flashy suits and recognizable goatee, slicked-back hair and mullet, which endeared him to hockey fans worldwide. He regularly worked alongside Levy and John Buccigross on ESPN's hockey coverage, including All-Star Games, Stanley Cup playoffs and the Cup Final.

"Barry was my best friend at ESPN," Buccigross wrote on social media Wednesday night. "A big brother figure of rock solid values. I am shook to my core. Barry gave his life to hockey and some of his ESPN family, like me, learned of his shocking death today while at a hockey rink in Las Vegas preparing for the upcoming season. Chilling and fitting -- the rink was Barry's home. A more beloved ESPN institution there has not been. We love you, Barry. Forever."

Added Levy: "For more than 30 years Barry was the unquestioned face/voice of hockey in the United States. He was a man of the people, a family man, a part of my family. Tonight I'll toast to the kid from Kelvington who made it big but never forgot his roots. Now he can drink all the Bud Lights, smoke all the cigars and play all the rounds of golf he wants to. Barry Melrose was the best of us."

At the time of Melrose's retirement, Gretzky, The Great One, paid tribute to him with the greatest of compliments: "Hockey is more than a game, it's a community -- a finely tuned orchestra -- and Barry was our conductor."

The Kings hired Melrose in 1992, and with Gretzky leading the way, they made a memorable playoff run, reaching the Cup Final before losing to the Montreal Canadiens in five games.

Rob Blake, a Hockey Hall of Fame defenseman, played for Melrose during that time, and after learning of his death Wednesday, he recalled their days together.

"He was just a terrific person to be in charge of our team," Blake told ESPN. "A real big personality and he was a pleasure. He loved the game of hockey -- the bright lights in L.A. were nothing for him when he got there."

Blake said he wasn't surprised when Melrose made a successful pivot to television.

"What he was teaching us about the game of hockey, he was teaching on TV," Blake said. "He got to promote the game for a number of years at a very high level. It was great."

Tony Granato, another former King, added: "He could light up a room. He could make people hear his voice and then you turn around and wonder what else he was going to say? There was no phoniness to him. He just was himself."

Melrose, who was from rural Kelvington, Saskatchewan, began his coaching career in 1987, when he led the Medicine Hat Tigers to the WHL's Memorial Cup title. He also coached the Seattle Thunderbirds for the 1988-89 season and the Adirondack Red Wings of the American Hockey League for three seasons (1989 to 1992), winning the Calder Cup championship in 1991.

During his 11 years as a player, Melrose appeared in 335 career games as a defenseman in the NHL with the Winnipeg Jets, Toronto Maple Leafs and Detroit Red Wings (1979 to 1986). He also played three seasons with Cincinnati in the WHA (1976 to 1979) -- the last teaming with a young Mark Messier.

He finished with 10 goals, 33 points and 728 penalty minutes in 300 NHL career games. His WHA totals were five goals, 32 points and 343 penalty minutes in 178 games.

"From the flowing locks of his distinctive mullet to the flared lapels of his trademark long suit coats, Barry Melrose cut an unmistakable figure whenever you were fortunate enough to run into him at a rink or catch him on your television screen," NHL commissioner Gary Bettman said. "You were even more fortunate if you engaged him in conversation or listened to his analysis because he never failed to boost your love of the game of hockey."

Melrose is survived by his wife, Cindy, and two sons, Tyrell and Adrien.

ESPN's Greg Wyshynski contributed to this report.

stories.headline: EuroLeague sets Oct. 5 to vote on role in NBA Europe project
stories.summary: EuroLeague owners are set to meet on Oct. 5 in Milan, Italy to discuss whether to accept the NBA proposal and allow the league to be absorbed into NBA Europe or continue to operate as a separate league.
stories.body:
The EuroLeague owners are set to meet on Oct. 5 in Milan, Italy to discuss their future role in the NBA's October 2027 planned launch of a new European basketball league.

EuroLeague Basketball CEO Chus Bueno said the organization would compete alongside NBA Europe should they not form a partnership with the proposed FIBA-backed project.

"If we don't get a deal in Europe, we're going to compete in Europe ... that's the discussion that we had internally, and if we have to, we're ready," Bueno told Reuters last week.

"It has to be a partnership that works for both of us, not just for one of us.

"We know the NBA ⁠can help operate things, so we should follow the NBA and they should follow the local IP [brand value] of clubs because they've been on the ground for 100 years and they can bring also a lot to the table for the NBA."

The NBA has received finalized bids from more than 20 groups, sources familiar with the negotiations told ESPN in late June.

Viable groups submitted bids in all 12 target cities, sources said, with multiple bids topping $1 billion in select markets, including from more than 20 existing basketball and football clubs, many of which are EuroLeague teams.

The NBA Board of Governors meet next week.

According to Gazzetta dello Sport, the Oct. 5 owners' meeting is for EuroLeague clubs to discuss whether to accept the NBA proposal and allow the league to be absorbed into NBA Europe, or whether to decline and continue operating a league separate from NBA Europe.

"If you have two leagues ... this is going to create fragmentation of the value, institutionally but also commercially, in media rights, fan attendance," Bueno told Reuters.

"We both said that if we don't have a deal, we have to keep going with our plans. So, as you know, they keep going through the process, and I keep going with my plan."

NBA Europe would feature 16 teams competing in a round-robin regular season and a multi-round playoff format, which will culminate with a finals.

Christo Stavropoulos, manager of Olimpia Milano, the club that will host the Oct. 5 meeting said the NBA's absorption of EuroLeague is not a given.

"If another competition is added, fragmentation will follow. For me, as I've said a thousand times, the ideal would be to collaborate with the NBA," Stavropoulos told Gazzetta dello Sport. "But it can't be taken for granted that it will happen. If it doesn't happen now, those of us in the EuroLeague have very clear ideas about what we want for the future.

"You know: franchises, more teams in the competition ... basketball in Europe is growing a lot, the EuroLeague is growing. Many teams want to join; the coming years are going to be very important.

"We will make important decisions about the future at the board meeting. If it's without the NBA , so be it. We have our own path prepared."

During the Oct. 5 meeting, eight new league franchise are expected to be approved for operation, part of Bueno's EuroLeague expansion plan.

Should EuroLeague opt out of NBA Europe, Bueno's plan includes a large-scale transition to a closed franchise system and the expansion of the league to 24 teams, with 21 permanent franchises securing their spots for the 2027-2028 season.

stories.headline: Max Verstappen admits to McLaren, Mercedes talks before 'following heart' with Red Bull stay
stories.summary: Max Verstappen has admitted to serious talks with McLaren and Mercedes before agreeing his Red Bull extension last month.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen has admitted to serious talks with McLaren and Mercedes before agreeing his Red Bull extension last month.

Verstappen ended a long period of uncertainty about his future with the new Red Bull deal, announced ahead of his home race, the Dutch Grand Prix, which overwrote a deal lasting until 2028 with one running through to the end of 2030.

The existence of escape clauses in his old deal had allowed rumours of moves elsewhere to spread.

Verstappen has acknowledged that he explored options with rival teams before committing to a longer deal.

"Of course, any kind of chat you take seriously," Verstappen said in a BBC Sport interview when asked about how serious talks were with McLaren and Mercedes. "They're all very respectful chats. There's nothing wrong with that."

Verstappen has been with Red Bull for his entire Formula 1 career. The company signed him to a developmental deal in 2014 before handing him a debut with junior team Toro Rosso the following season.

He memorably won for Red Bull on his first appearance with the team after replacing Daniil Kvyat at the 2016 Spanish Grand Prix.

He spent five seasons at the team before winning his first championship in 2021, the first of four consecutive titles.

- Spanish Grand Prix: Everything you need to know about the Madring

- Red Bull sign Kimi Raikkonen's son Robin, 11

- Leclerc advice for Max vs. 100 drivers: Don't crash!

Verstappen pointed out he could have left Red Bull in those fallow years and ultimately opted to stay this time around as he believes Red Bull can be contenders again in future.

"I felt that staying was, for me, the right choice," he said. "You have to follow your heart. I could have run away very early on in my Red Bull career and gone somewhere else to try and win. If you have a little bit of patience, you do end up winning. I feel like that's my approach now as well."

Part of the uncertainty around Verstappen's future had been linked to his discontent with Formula 1's controversial new hybrid engines, which have shifted a lot of emphasis onto energy management and deployment.

Verstappen has labelled this "anti-racing" and likened the new F1 to Mario Kart.

F1 is making tweaks to the engines in 2027 and 2028 to lessen the importance of the electrical elements and Verstappen hopes this will lead to an improvement in how the racing feels.

"Hoping that it will be better in the future," he said. "Accepting where we are at the moment. Still the love for the sport. Not at the moment the driving. But the love for the sport.

"I love competition, naturally. I just hope that in the coming years, towards 2030, it can only get better. And to start to make the best of it, because these are the rules for the next four or five years."

stories.headline: How Holbrook inspired Newcastle's remarkable turnaround
stories.summary: Newcastle have scored an extra 12.3 points per game in 2026 compared to last year's wooden-spoon season, making for the fourth greatest improvement in history.
stories.body:
It took just one meeting for Justin Holbrook to start providing the belief for the fourth greatest attacking turnaround in Australian rugby league history.

With Newcastle players arriving for day one of pre-season, Holbrook's first move was to make clear last year's wooden spoon was irrelevant.

"There was obviously a lot of outside noise," five-eighth Fletcher Sharpe recalled.

"But Justin sat us down and said: 'Look, I don't really care about what happened last year - it's a new year and looking at the squad in front of me, I know we can take it all out'."

Brought in after Adam O'Brien's Newcastle exit, Holbrook immediately made his mark.

"He said we had to come together and buy into a style. And we can win the comp," added halfback Sandon Smith, who had worked with Holbrook at the Sydney Roosters.

"We bought in from November 1.

"It wasn't a moment throughout the season where we thought, 'Oh wait we can actually do this'. It was built into us from the first day."

Ahead of Friday night's elimination final against South Sydney, Holbrook's Newcastle turnaround is statistically one of the greatest in history.

And at the centre of it all is Newcastle's attack, with players quick to heap praise on assistant Stephen Hales.

Newcastle were kept scoreless in 11 halves of football in 2025, and had the NRL's worst attack.

Such is the improvement, the Knights are scoring an extra 12.3 points per game this year.

Only three sides in the game's 118-year history have had a greater increase, with Parramatta in 2001 the last side to have such a dramatic rise.

While Newcastle scored five tries from the other side of halfway last year, this year they have the most in the NRL with 30.

And 63 tries have also originated from outside the attacking 20-metre zone, compared to 18 last season.

"It's a fun style to play," Sharpe said.

"I remember at the start it seemed expansive and off the cuff, but the whole team bought into it.

"It allows our strike players on the edges to get plenty of ball and do their thing.

"It's probably a style not everyone plays, so it gives a difference and plenty of variety too, which you need at this time of year."

Remarkably, Newcastle are having less play-the-balls on the opposition tryline and running similar metres per game to last year.

But they are far more efficient and have a willingness to shift more often from their own end, giving their fast and powerful outside backs early ball to play with.

Wingers Dom Young and Greg Marzhew have 62 linebreaks and 44 tries between them.

Kalyn Ponga remains at the heart of the attack, but hooker Phoenix Crossland believes the rise of Sharpe has taken some pressure off the Newcastle No.1.

"We're attacking nothing like we used to last year," Crossland said.

"That happens with new coaches and fresh ideas, with boys buying into our system."

Impressive too is the fact the rise has come with Newcastle rarely at full strength, with Sharpe, Ponga and the now-injured Dylan Brown having stints out.

"The strength of our coaching staff is just letting individuals express themselves," Ponga said.

"Every team's got systems, but what they've done a good job of is just giving you that belief that you can play your footy.

"That's just the way that they frame everything up, that there's no limit on what you can be."

Parramatta (2001): +14.0

Newcastle (2026): +12.3

stories.headline: Ødegaard: Arsenal on 'another level' after Champions League win continues unbeaten start
stories.summary: Martin Ødegaard has said Arsenal are "on another level" this season after winning the Premier League title gave Mikel Arteta's side a new level of confidence.
stories.body:
Martin Ødegaard has said Arsenal are "on another level" this season after winning the Premier League title gave Mikel Arteta's side a new level of confidence.

The Arsenal captain scored the winner as the Gunners opened their Champions League campaign with a 1-0 victory over Napoli at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on Wednesday. Ødegaard struck from the edge of the area in the 75th minute, his fourth goal in five appearances this season, after the visitors had fluffed a number of chances.

Arsenal, who also reached last season's Champions League final, have won all five of their games this season, while all 10 of their goals have come from open play. Ødegaard was named player of the match in Naples after continuing his impressive start to the campaign.

"I think we feel different. I think we feel a lot stronger this year and I've said it many times," Ødegaard told CBS Sports. "I said it also after the season when we finished second, you got to learn from it. You got to take the experiences.

"And of course it's the same when you win and it's a different experience. It gives you different kind of confidence. And I can feel that now in the whole team-- we play with a different confidence and I feel like we're on another level this season.

"So yeah, I think it made us a lot stronger and I feel like the team is just growing and growing and we're getting better and the hunger is there. So that's great to see after winning that we want to do it again and we want more."

Ødegaard endured an injury-hit campaign last season but played a key role during Arsenal's title run-in, before carrying his form into the World Cup and the start of the new season.

"I think the main change is I'm on the pitch and I feel good and I feel fit," the Norwegian said. "As I said, I think last season was a big struggle. I had a lot of injuries, a lot of bad luck, couldn't really find the rhythm.

"You're out for a while, then you come back in and then maybe you need a few games to get really sharp. But then I had another incident, a lot of situations like this, and sometimes you play when you're not feeling 100%.

"So it was hard, but now I feel good. Obviously winning the league here last season and then going into the World Cup felt really good in the World Cup, had a good tournament there and then now took it into the new season. So I'm really happy."

- Olley: Who needs a forward? Arsenal might, but not while Ødegaard keeps delivering

- Mikel Arteta: Martin Ødegaard 'decisive' in Champions League win at Napoli

- Napoli 0-1 Arsenal: As it happened as Gunners continue perfect start

Arteta was encouraged by the availability of his forwards and the tenacity of his squad at a tough away ground.

"As I said many times last year, that's where we missed so many attacking players that now they are playing their feet and they're all available to play," the Arsenal mananger said.

"I'm really pleased just to talk about what we've done today on the pitch against a great opponent in a really difficult context and environment here in the stadium. And we show such a personality and quality today to win the game."

stories.headline: No panic: McVee in as Dockers vow to right the wrongs
stories.summary: Fremantle players succumbed to Hawthorn's pressure in last week's qualifying final flop, but Justin Longmuir is backing his team to right the wrongs.
stories.body:
Defender Judd McVee has been recalled and Fremantle's players are being urged not to panic as the Dockers brace for their date with destiny in Friday night's semi-final blockbuster against Geelong.

McVee has been dropped twice over the past month, but the former Demon is being backed to rediscover his best form in the pressure-cooker environment of a cut-throat final at a sold-out Optus Stadium in Perth.

The 23-year-old will replace the injured Brandon Walker (ankle), with coach Justin Longmuir also confirming out-of-favour ruckman Sean Darcy couldn't be considered after copping a knock to his knee in the WAFL last week.

Fremantle stars such as Josh Treacy, Shai Bolton, Hayden Young, Pat Voss and Jye Amiss were heavily criticised after last week's 32-point home qualifying-final loss to Hawthorn.

But Longmuir is backing his players to rebound strongly, and he knows first-hand what it takes to recover from a qualifying-final loss.

Longmuir was part of the Fremantle side that lost to Adelaide by 30 points in the 2006 qualifying final, before coming out firing the next week to defeat Melbourne by 28 points in a semi-final.

"Don't panic," Longmuir said of his message.

"We had some players that weren't up to their best last week, and multiple players that weren't up to the best.

"But they didn't let me down. We finished top of the ladder, gave ourselves two chances.

"We're one win away from prelim, same as what we were last week.

"So there's a lot of optimism in the group, a lot of trust and faith that our best footy is good enough, and I'm sure you'll see a different team.

"The players are keen to get out there and right some wrongs."

Fremantle succumbed to Hawthorn's intense pressure, leading to players firing off panicked handballs instead of playing with freedom and taking on the tackler.

McVee is set to play on either Shaun Mannagh, Brad Close or Gryan Miers in what looms as a crucial match-up given Fremantle's struggles to contain smaller forwards this season.

Longmuir has told McVee to trust himself.

"When he's playing his best footy, he's playing on instinct and trusting his ability," Longmuir said.

"You've probably seen his contest drop away a little bit and the pressure of others playing really well at Peel has found him out of the team.

"But when he's playing his best footy, he's working with his teammates well, he's trusting his read of the ball, and then trusting himself in the contest.

"The rest can flow off that."

Geelong enter the match full of confidence following their 33-point elimination-final win over in-form Carlton.

Patrick Dangerfield wound back the clock with five goals, but there are big questions about how well the 36-year-old will be able to back-up that performance.

The fitness of Jeremy Cameron and Max Holmes have also been in the spotlight following their recent injuries, but Geelong's vastly superior September experience looms as a key advantage against a Dockers outfit that have lost three finals on the trot.

stories.headline: 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup: Team USA and quarterfinal preview
stories.summary: The U.S. women and France remain front-runners as the knockout stage arrives in Berlin, but who else has impressed?
stories.body:
BERLIN -- The quarterfinals are set for the 2026 FIBA World Cup, with eight teams still in the hunt for a spot on the podium in Germany this weekend.

The United States, France and Belgium are the only countries still undefeated, though Italy tested the U.S. women in their second group game. The Americans eked out a 55-52 victory, their lowest-scoring World Cup performance since 1971.

Those three teams, along with Spain (2-1), punched their tickets to Thursday's quarterfinals. On Tuesday, Hungary beat Japan and Germany topped Korea to also secure spots in the final eight. On Wednesday, China secured its quarterfinal berth with a win over Puerto Rico, and the final spot went to Australia, which held off Italy in the final qualification showdown.

Here's what you need to know about how the United States has performed and how the rest of the field ranks as we turn the page to the knockout rounds.

Jump to:

AUS | BEL | CHN | FRA

GER | HUN | ESP | USA

Power Rankings | Team USA analysis

In what areas has Team USA been most impressive?
As is the case with other U.S. women's teams, the depth of talent continues to stand out. Coach Kara Lawson has started the five returning senior team players -- Napheesa Collier, Kahleah Copper, Chelsea Gray, Breanna Stewart and Jackie Young -- each game this tournament, meaning the likes of Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers, Aliyah Boston and Angel Reese are coming off the bench -- an enviable position to every other country in this event.

Watching the United States at its best -- as ESPN colleague Michael Voepel put it during the 94-61 win over China -- is like watching a movie in which every role is played by an Oscar winner. And if the U.S. women are getting stops, getting out in transition, sharing the ball and making the opponent pay on the other end, it's world-class basketball.

For the most part, each player on the roster has had some strong moments so far this tournament -- even after the vets struggled mightily most of the Italy game, they were the ones who made winning plays down the stretch to ensure the United States remained undefeated. The Young and Turnt crew don't always get everything perfect, but they have shown they belong. Having so many newcomers will pay dividends in the future in terms of experience, but Team USA will need them now to ensure the team goes home with a fifth consecutive World Cup gold medal.

Where have the Americans struggled?
The U.S. women aren't immune from defensive breakdowns, which isn't shocking given the team came together so last minute and chemistry is developing in real time. But the biggest concern is how the USA will generate offense when things don't come easily.

It's unlikely the U.S. women will score 55 points and shoot below 30% from the field again this tournament (or maybe even this decade) as they did against Italy. But the performance was eerily reminiscent of the France game from the 2024 Olympics, another close call but with a gold medal on the line.

The U.S. women's efficiency in this tournament has been much lower than we're used to seeing: 43.4%, ranking eighth, and a 29% accuracy from the 3-point arc (11th in the field) -- all while not generating a ton of looks from deep (23 per game).

This is where not having A'ja Wilson and Kelsey Plum -- two players very capable of going to get a bucket -- really hurts. Which players, or what combinations, will create offense if things become stagnant?

During TNT's FIBA World Cup studio show, three-time U.S. Olympic gold medalist Tina Charles said after the Italy game that she didn't see anyone pull Team USA together and essentially say, "Enough, get it together, let's end this now." With no Diana Taurasi or Wilson around, that's Stewart's or Gray's role moving forward, with their play on the court and in how they lead their teammates.

1. United States (3-0)

Next opponent: Quarterfinals vs. Hungary (5:30 a.m. ET Thursday)

How they've looked: The U.S. women are right where everyone expected them to be: undefeated and playing in the quarterfinals. But their path so far hasn't been without some struggles. Though two of the United States' group games -- victories over China and Czechia by 30-plus points each -- reflected the dominance we've come to expect, the 55-52 win against Italy neared catastrophe. It was Team USA's smallest margin of victory in the World Cup since 1979 and its first World Cup game decided by single digits since 2010.

The U.S. women rebounded by scoring more first-half points against Czechia (57) than they totaled against Italy, and they hope to bring that momentum into the knockout rounds. Eight players are averaging at least six points, and no one is averaging more than 12 (Young is the team leader with 11.3 PPG).

2. France (3-0)

How they've looked: France was considered the top challenger to U.S. entering the World Cup and still appears to be the biggest contender. In fact, the French have a strong argument to top this ranking, having outscored opponents by a tournament-best 127 points. Their defense gave the U.S. women fits at the Paris Olympics, but so far in Berlin, Les Bleues have scored at least 95 points each game, with dynamic duo Williams (the tournament's leading scorer with 18.7 PPG) and Johannes combining for 36 PPG.

How they've looked: Belgium predictably came out of Group C unscathed, winning each of its first three games by double figures. And just as expected, Meesseman has been one of the best players in the tournament, averaging 18.3 points, 8.0 rebounds, 5.3 assists and 1.7 blocks. Belgium is the better team on paper, but Germany will be playing with extra pride and a boisterous home crowd behind it in the quarterfinals.

How they've looked: Spain looked poised to be one of the more exciting teams to take the court in Berlin but enters the quarterfinals with a 2-1 record after suffering a stunning loss to Mali in the second game of group play. The Spanish can still get to the podium for their fourth time in as many tournament appearances, but that kind of run would surely necessitate their young duo of Martin (17.3 PPG) and Fam (12.3 PPG) to play beyond their years in big moments.

How they've looked: It hasn't been the easiest ride for Sandy Brondello's team. Already missing Sami Whitcomb because of injury before the World Cup, Australia lost Smith 12 minutes into its first game in Berlin. She hasn't played since and on Thursday was ruled out for the remainder of the World Cup. After taking care of Puerto Rico and Turkiye, the Australians kept up with Belgium (a 80-68 loss) but had to beat a gritty Italy squad for a spot in the final eight.

How they've looked: The World Cup has been a roller coaster for China. The team was routed by the U.S. in its first game, nearly lost to Czechia the next time out before pulling away in overtime and then put together a convincing 20-point win over Italy to close group play. China beat Puerto Rico on Wednesday in a qualifying game for the quarterfinals, and France -- a tough matchup -- awaits in the quarters. Han Xu has been their superstar, averaging 17.3 points, 11.3 rebounds and 2.7 assists.

7. Germany (3-1)

How they've looked: After being trounced by Spain to open the tournament, Germany has won three straight, including Tuesday's clobbering of Korea to clinch a spot in the quarters. A quarterfinal appearance is a good step for a program appearing in only its second World Cup, but Germany is hoping it can capitalize on being a host and having a talented squad. Buhner has had a strong tournament, averaging a team-high 15.3 points.

8. Hungary (3-1)

How they've looked: It has been a memorable World Cup for Hungary, which is appearing in the event for the first time since 1998. The team was throttled by France to start the tournament but hasn't lost since on its way to the quarterfinals. Though Juhász carried Hungary through group play with averages of 17 points and 12.3 rebounds, Reka Lelik was the team's star Tuesday, finishing with a game-high 23 points, eight rebounds and four assists against Japan.

stories.headline: Messi tracker: Goals, assists, key moments in 2026
stories.summary: ESPN provides game-by-game analysis of Lionel Messi's performances for Inter Miami and Argentina.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will aim for more success in 2026. His Inter Miami side captured its first MLS Cup title last season and will look to defend it -- and add further silverware too -- in its first season at Nu Stadium, the club's new home.

Messi also captained Argentina as they fell just one step short of defending their FIFA World Cup crown, losing 1-0 in extra time to Spain in the final of what could be his last tournament.

As the 39-year-old continues to feature for both club and country, ESPN will track his performances game-by-game, providing stats and analysis each time he pulls on a Herons or Albiceleste jersey.

Messi's 2026 tally:

Games played: 35
Goals: 31
Assists: 14

Sep. 9: Chicago Fire 1-1 Inter Miami

Two or Europe's greatest club players took center stage in one of the United States' most iconic American football stadiums on Wednesday -- and a record crowd came out to watch.

Ex-Bayern Munich and Barcelona star Robert Lewandowski scored a trademark acrobatic goal in the 10th minute to give the Fire an early lead at the NFL home of the Chicago Bears.

But Inter Miami drew level shortly after halftime when Casemiro, another of the game's stars with a long history of playing in Europe before moving to MLS, headed home a Messi cross from a corner kick to make it 1-1.

The assist was Messi's league-leading 13th of the season. He also has league 18 goals and is the first player in MLS history with 30-plus goal contributions in three separate seasons.

Sep. 5: Inter Miami 2-2 Atlanta United
Messi was not as effective as he was in the previous matchup, but he did get an assist for Casemiro's opening goal. However, his team was unable to win as they had to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw.

August 29: Inter Miami 7-1 CF Montréal

Fans were treated to a Messi masterclass on Saturday as the Argentine magician registered four goals and an assist to help Miami to a club-record 7-1 victory over CF Montréal.

Messi scored with a deflected free kick in the 40th minute before netting after a stunning solo run in the 52nd. After supplying an assist to Luis Suárez, the 39-year-old then completed his hat trick and with a delicate chip over the goalkeeper with seven minutes of regulation time remaining.

He wasn't done yet.

Deep into stoppage time, Messi lined up a free kick and dispatched it with trademark precision into the top corner of the net. Legendary stuff.

August 22: Inter Miami 2-1 Toronto FC

Messi's 14th MLS goal of the season wasn't enough to prevent Inter Miami from slumping to their fourth loss in their last five games, losing 2-1 to Toronto FC at Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Messi found the net with a first-time finish from a Rodrigo De Paul through-ball with eight minutes remaining, but the home side's late rally fell short of salvaging a much-needed draw to bolster the Herons' pursuit of first-placed Nashville SC in the Eastern Conference.

August 19: Inter Miami 2-2 Philadelphia Union

Messi is back scoring goals, but unfortunately, his Miami side is not back to winning ways. The Argentine scored Miami's second goal of the night as both teams finished with 10 men. Miami are now winless in their last four matches.

August 15: Nashville SC 4-1 Inter Miami
It was not the best night for Messi in Tennessee. The Argentine missed yet another penalty -- his third straight for club and country -- and they suffered a heavy 4-1 loss to their Eastern Conference rivals. However, he did get an assist for Telasco Segovia's equalizer at halftime before Miami lost control in the second half.

August 12: Inter Miami 2-3 Club León
Just days after the passing of his father, Messi came off the bench in the second half to try to help Miami continue in the Leagues Cup after they were leading 1-0. However, it ended in a 3-2 loss which saw them eliminated in the league phase after a second straight loss, coming off defeat to Monterrey last weekend with Messi away at the memorial for his father.

August 5: Inter Miami 4-2 Atlético de San Luis

Lionel Messi made his first start for Inter Miami since returning from the World Cup and picked up right where he left off, scoring a stellar pair of goals to guide his team to a come-from-behind 4-2 rout of Atlético de San Luis in its first game of the 2026 Leagues Cup.

Messi's first goal was an exquisite volley, redirecting Noah Allen's cross from the left flank while running at full speed. Miami's third goal of the opening half -- and Messi's second on the night -- came on the back of some intricate buildup play with Allen once again setting up his team captain, this time in the center of the area where he tiptoed through two defenders and buried a close-range strike past Andrés Sánchez.

The goal made Messi the all-time leading scorer in Leagues Cup history with 14, one ahead of LAFC's Denis Bouanga since the expanded competition began in 2023.

August 1: Inter Miami 2-2 Columbus Crew
Messi made his return to action for Inter Miami on Saturday, 13 days after tasting defeat with Argentina in the World Cup final. The Miami talisman started on the substitutes' bench before being introduced in the 53rd minute of the Herons' 2-2 draw with the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in Miami.

July 19: Spain 1-0 AET Argentina

Sunday proved to be a bridge too far for both Messi and Argentina, falling in extra time to Spain in the World Cup final.

With La Roja controlling the match basically from start to finish -- Argentina didn't register a shot on target during regulation time -- Messi had few opportunities to impact the game. Indeed, the 39-year-old was given a 3/10 in ESPN's post-match player ratings.

Still, as Mark Ogden points out, the 2026 tournament was a memorable one for Messi and cemented his status as the GOAT, if it were ever in doubt.

July 15: England 1-2 Argentina
Messi made another statement in his 205th appearance for Argentina, this time in his first-ever match against England in a World Cup semifinal. With so much at stake for both nations, Messi once again proved decisive despite not getting on the scoresheet.

He first provided the assist for Enzo Fernández's superb strike to level the match in the second half before delivering a pinpoint cross for Lautaro Martínez's headed winner, sending the reigning champions into yet another World Cup final after another dramatic encounter.

Messi has now recorded either a goal or an assist in all seven of Argentina's matches at this World Cup, and he will have the opportunity to lift the trophy for a second time when Argentina face Spain in Sunday's final in New Jersey.

July 11: Argentina 3-1 Switzerland
It was a relatively quiet night by Messi's standards as his goalscoring streak came to an end, but his influence on the match stayed the same. He set up Alexis Mac Allister's opening goal for Argentina against Switzerland, and although the match went to extra time, the defending champions won 3-1 thanks to two late goals in the second half of extra time.

Messi's quest to retain the World Cup now continues into the semifinals, where Argentina will face England for the first time in over 20 years. The clash in Atlanta -- one of international soccer's most storied rivalries -- will decide a spot in the final.

July 7: Argentina 3-2 Egypt
It was another dramatic outing for Messi and Argentina, who rallied from a 2-0 deficit to defeat Egypt 3-2 in Atlanta and book their place in the World Cup quarterfinals. As is so often the case, Messi was at the center of the action. Minutes after Egypt opened the scoring, he missed another penalty, but he quickly made amends by setting up Cristian Romero for Argentina's first goal. Messi then scored the equalizer -- his eighth goal of the tournament -- before Enzo Fernández completed the comeback with the winner. Argentina will now face Switzerland in Kansas City for a place in the semifinals.

July 3: Argentina 3-2 Cape Verde
Messi suffered a major scare in Miami Gardens on Friday evening in the round of 32, but it ultimately ended well for Argentina. He opened the scoring with his seventh goal of the tournament, extending his World Cup tally to 20 goals while finding the net in a record eighth consecutive World Cup match. Cape Verde twice fought back -- once in the second half and again in extra time -- but the world champions eventually prevailed 3-2 after extra time to book a meeting in the round of 16 with Egypt.

June 27: Jordan 1-3 Argentina
Messi didn't play the full 90 minutes in Argentina's 3-1 win over an already-eliminated Jordan, but he still made his mark during a 30-minute cameo in Texas. The 39-year-old scored a free kick for his sixth goal of the tournament and his 19th career World Cup goal, becoming the first player ever to score in seven consecutive World Cup matches. Even at 39, he's still got it.

June 22: Argentina 2-0 Austria
Another chapter in an already unparalleled career. Lionel Messi scored twice in Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria to help his team qualify for the round of 32 and become the outright leading goalscorer in men's and women's FIFA World Cup history with 18 goals. After missing an early penalty, he responded by breaking Miroslav Klose's 12-year-old record and then added a second late on to break Marta's record. All just two days before turning 39.

June 16: Argentina 3-0 Algeria
In his 200th appearance for Argentina and sixth World Cup, Lionel Messi sent a message to the world just days before his 39th birthday: he still has it. His first-ever World Cup hat trick powered Argentina to victory in their group-stage opener, while his 16th tournament goal saw him draw level with Miroslav Klose for the most goals in World Cup history.

June 9: Argentina 3-0 Iceland

Messi, working his way back from muscle fatigue ahead of the start of the World Cup, came on in the 70th minute of a pre-tournament friendly in Auburn, Alabama and scored from the penalty spot right afterward.

It was Messi's 911th career goal for club and country and 117th goal for Argentina and made him the oldest scorer in the country's soccer history.

May 24: Inter Miami 6-4 Philadelphia Union

Messi registered two assists in a scintillating performance against Philadelphia on Sunday but, unfortunately, no one was focused on results come the end of the game.

That's because, in the very last game before the World Cup, Messi left the field in the 73rd minute and headed straight to the locker room after grabbing his left thigh.

Now, supporters around the world are holding their collective breath while they wait and see if the injury has scuppered the 38-year-old's chance of appearing at a sixth World Cup.

May 13: FC Cincinnati 3-5 Inter Miami

Two goals and one assist marked yet another spectacular contribution from Miami superstar Messi on Wednesday. The Argentine magician was instrumental as the Herons fought back from 3-2 down to eventually beat Cincinnati 5-3 at TQL Stadium in Ohio.

May 9: Toronto FC 2-4 Inter Miami

It was a day of star power. Not only were Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez and Sergio Reguilón all on the score sheet for the Herons, so was Messi -- and he added a pair of assists, too.

While Miami has yet to taste victory at its new home, it continues to take care of business on the road. Saturday's win in Toronto extended the club's unbeaten record away from home in 2026 to seven games, picking up six wins and one draw in the first few months of the season.

May 2: Inter Miami 3-4 Orlando City

Messi notched a goal and an assist on Saturday in what ended up being an astonishing collapse for Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Herons were leading 3-0 after Messi's classy 33rd-minute strike, but gifted the visitors four goals -- including a Martín Ojeda hat trick -- to once again miss out on a victory at their new home ground. Orlando's comeback from three goals down marks only the third time in MLS history that a team has claimed all three points after trailing by three or more goals.

As for Messi's Miami, only twice has an MLS team had a longer winless run -- now up to four for the Herons -- to open up a new stadium.

April 25: Inter Miami 1-1 New England Revolution
Messi again failed to get on the scoresheet as Miami put in a fatigued second-half performance that saw them come from a goal down against New England. It was another draw -- and another game without a win at their new home, Nu Stadium.

April 22: Real Salt Lake 0-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists from Messi as Miami visited America First Field on Wednesday, but the fans did get treated to sumptuous strikes nonetheless.

Rodrigo De Paul's opener in the 80th-minute was stunning curler from outside the box and then, almost immediately after the restart, Luis Suarez made it 2-0 with a well-struck volley.

The victory moves Inter Miami into outright second in the MLS Eastern Conference.

April 18: Colorado Rapids 2-3 Inter Miami

Another moment of Messi magic bagged all three points for Inter Miami on Saturday.

With scores level in the 79th minute, the Argentine icon danced his way past a number of Colorado defenders before curling home an outrageous effort into the far corner.

The strike -- Messi's second of the match after converting a penalty in the first half -- helped Miami to their first win under interim coach Guillermo Hoyos.

Hoyos, who had been serving as club's sporting director, took over coaching duties after Javier Mascherano unexpectedly left the club due to personal reasons last week.

April 11: Inter Miami 2-2 Red Bull New York
Miami and Messi are still waiting for a first win at Nu Stadium after a 2-2 draw with Red Bull New York on Saturday night.

Messi didn't register a goal or assist, but did help set up Germán Berterame's second-half strike that gave Inter Miami its first lead at its new home ground, but 17-year-old Adri Mehmeti's first career goal in the 77th minute secured a point for the visitors.

April 4: Inter Miami 2-2 Austin FC
Inter Miami opened Nu Stadium the only way it knows how: With a Messi goal. The No. 10 began the move in trademark style with a left-footed pass to a teammate before moving past a defender and arriving in the box at just the right time to head past goalkeeper Brad Stuver.

March 31: Argentina 5-0 Zambia
It was the last day of the month and perhaps the last game for Messi playing for Argentina playing in his native country, but they put on a show defeating the African side Zambia 5-0. Messi scored the second goal for Lionel Scaloni's side as focus will shift now to Miami until the beginning of the World Cup.

March 27: Argentina 2-1 Mauritania
In his first game for his country in 2026, Messi only played the second half as Argentina won 2-1 against Mauritania at the mythical La Bombonera in Buenos Aires, as the World Cup champions continue to prepare to defend their title this summer in North America.

March 22: NYCFC 2-3 Inter Miami

It was a thrilling encounter in the Bronx, as the Argentine star helped his team to a 3-2 win over NYCFC, which also included another trademark free kick goal, now beginning his course for potentially 1,000 career goals. Only 99 goals left!

March 18: Inter Miami 1-1 Nashville SC

Messi may have made history on Wednesday night, becoming just the second men's player in history to score 900 career goals, but it wasn't enough to seal Miami's progress in the Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Argentina legend found the back of the net in the seventh minute at Chase Stadium, but his strike was cancelled out by Nashville's Cristian Espinoza -- sealing the Herons' tournament exit on the away goals rule.

March 11: Nashville SC 0-0 Inter Miami
A drab night for Messi and Co. in the Concacaf Champions Cup. Plenty of possession but few shots on target mean that the Herons will return to Chase Stadium know a win will be needed to ensure progression.

March 7: D.C. United 1-2 Inter Miami

It was quite an eventful week for Messi. Just days before Miami's match against D.C. United, Messi and the entire squad visited the White House and met President Donald Trump and were eager to put on a show for the sold-out crowd of over 70,000 at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium.

And they did just that, with a 2-1 win over D.C. United. Messi, of course, scored Miami's second and is now one goal away from 900 career goals.

March 1: Orlando City 2-4 Inter Miami

Well, that blip didn't last long! Messi and Miami roared back into life with a 4-2 thrashing of Orlando on Sunday thanks to the 38-year-old's wizardry.

Things looked ominous for the Herons after the first 45 minutes, down 2-0 and looking on course to start the MLS season with two bleak losses.

But two goals and an assist from Messi in the second half dragged the visitors back in the game and helped secure Miami their first points of the season.

Feb. 21: LAFC 3-0 Inter Miami
Messi and Miami aimed to start 2026 firing on all cylinders, but it was the hosts who spoiled the defending MLS Cup champions' opener at the LA Coliseum. In front of a sellout crowd of 75,673 -- the second-highest attendance in MLS history -- Miami were outplayed, with LAFC's Denis Bouanga getting a goal and an assist in a convincing home victory.

The main talking point, however, emerged after the final whistle. Messi was initially reported to have gained unauthorized access to the officials' locker room after video circulated showing him near the area. However, it was later reported that no league policy had been violated and Messi was cleared of any wrongdoing. Miami will now turn its attention next weekend against fellow Florida side Orlando City.
